title: Strava Segment PR Near-Miss Tracker
dataSources: Strava API activities (`strava:activity`), Garmin Connect (`garmin:activity`), Fitbit Web API (`fitbit:activity`), Peloton workout history (`peloton:workout`), Zwift ride exports (`zwift:activity`).
app: Strava / Garmin Connect / Fitbit / Peloton / Zwift APIs and webhooks via Splunk HEC scripted inputs; GPX/FIT/CSV activity exports ingested as file inputs.

index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity has_segments=true

description: Finds the segments where you are repeatedly a few seconds short of a personal record, so you know exactly which efforts are one good day away from a breakthrough.
value: Near misses are motivating because they show fitness is already there; this list turns vague 'I think I'm close' feelings into specific targets.
implementation: Forward per-segment performance data from Strava; review the tightest near misses before your next hard session.
visualization: Leaderboard of segments with the smallest PR gaps.
detailedImplementation:
## Prerequisites

• **Splunk**: Splunk Enterprise ≥9.0 or Splunk Cloud — a single-instance home lab is fine. Create `index=personal` with 90–365 day retention (`indexes.conf`).
• **HEC token**: Settings → Data Inputs → HTTP Event Collector → New Token → index `personal`. Store the token in your connector's environment (never commit it to git).
• **Upstream product**: Strava — REST API or webhook → Splunk HEC scripted input.
• **Subcategory context**: Fitness & Activity Tracking — typical feeds: Strava API activities (`strava:activity`), Garmin Connect (`garmin:activity`), Fitbit Web API (`fitbit:activity`), Peloton workout history (`peloton:workout`), Zwift/TrainingPeaks exports..
• **Sourcetypes in this search**: `strava:activity`.
• **Network**: The connector host must reach both the vendor API/MQTT broker and your Splunk HEC port (8088/tcp).

## Step 1 — Configure data collection

Route **Strava** events into `index=personal` with `sourcetype=strava:activity`.

**Collection method:** REST API or webhook → Splunk HEC scripted input.

**Reference endpoint / path:** `GET https://www.strava.com/api/v3/athlete/activities`.

**Suggested poll interval:** 900s (or push via Strava webhook subscription).

**Key fields to extract:** `type, distance_km, moving_time_s, start_date, athlete_id`.

**Typical connector stack:** Strava / Garmin Connect / Fitbit / Peloton / Zwift APIs and webhooks via Splunk HEC scripted inputs; GPX/FIT/CSV activity exports ingested as files..

**Author notes:** Forward per-segment performance data from Strava; review the tightest near misses before your next hard session.


Example HEC payload shape:

```json
{"index": "personal", "sourcetype": "strava:activity", "event": { ... vendor fields ... }}
```

Verify ingestion with:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity earliest=-24h | head 20
```

## Step 2 — Create the search and alert

This search implements **Strava Segment PR Near-Miss Tracker** over `personal` data (primarily `sourcetype=strava:activity`) across the full search range. It applies numeric thresholds on `closest_gap` (> 0) after min — tune these constants to your household baseline.

**Fields this search depends on:** `closest_gap`, `segment_name`. Confirm each is populated before scheduling alerts.

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity has_segments=true
| stats min(pr_gap_seconds) as closest_gap, count as attempts by segment_name
| where closest_gap>0 AND closest_gap<=10
| sort closest_gap
```

## Step 3 — Validate

**(a) Compare to vendor UI:** Strava app → You → Activities list for the same week totals. Totals for the same day/week should match within connector lag (usually one poll interval).

**(b) Field presence:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity earliest=-7d
| head 50
| table closest_gap, segment_name
```

Every column the detection uses should be non-null on recent rows.

**(c) Volume sanity:**

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity earliest=-30d
| timechart span=1d count
```

Flatlines usually mean a broken token, expired OAuth refresh, or HEC URL change.

**(d) Threshold calibration:** Profile `closest_gap` before alerting:

```spl
index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity earliest=-30d
| stats perc50(closest_gap) AS p50 perc90(closest_gap) AS p90 perc99(closest_gap) AS p99 max(closest_gap) AS hi
```

## Step 4 — Operationalize

Create a companion dashboard titled `UC-25.1.16: Personal evidence` with the following panel layout:

**Panel 1 — Leaderboard Of Segments With The Smallest Pr Gaps (the key fields):** Configure according to standard Splunk visualization patterns for this panel type.


Time picker defaults: set to last 30 days with named presets for 24h, 7d, 30d, 90d, and 1y — the auditor needs all five windows without retyping. Enable scheduled PDF export for the full dashboard on the regulation's reporting cadence.

## Step 5 — Troubleshooting

**Strava — no Strava events / missing fields:** If `strava:activity` stops updating, re-check HEC token, index `personal`, and firewall to port 8088. Search `index=_internal sourcetype=splunkd group=http_event_collector` for rejection reasons. Confirm the Strava connector script is still running (`systemctl status` or cron log).

**Strava — NULL values in extracted fields:** The Strava JSON export shape drifted — compare a raw event (`index=personal sourcetype=strava:activity | head 1 | spath`) against the field names in Step 2. Re-map in the connector before changing the SPL.

**Strava — API error / auth denied (401/403):** Refresh tokens expire on most consumer APIs — re-authorize the scripted input, update `passwords.conf` / env vars, and verify the vendor developer app is not in sandbox mode.

**Strava — endpoint timeout / HTTP 429 throttling:** Back off the poll interval in the connector; Strava APIs often cap requests per 15 minutes on free tiers.

**Stale dashboard:** Confirm the saved search `dispatch.earliest_time` covers enough history for your `aggregation` buckets.
